Chapter 10—Living Out Loud: Sustaining Growth and Empowerment.
Let’s talk about what it really means to sustain the changes you’ve made, and how you can keep growing, day after day.
Growth isn’t something that happens just once—it’s a lifelong journey. It needs your attention, your reflection, and, above all, your willingness to adapt as you go.
When you’re living out loud, you’re showing up fully for your own life. You’re taking up space, speaking your truth, and going after what matters most to you. And you know what? You’re doing this without shrinking, or apologizing for who you are.
Let me share some gentle reminders that can help you keep that momentum going:
First, check in with yourself often. Ask: What do I need right now? Sometimes, just pausing to listen to your own needs can make all the difference.
Don’t forget to celebrate your progress, no matter how small. Every little win counts.
Keep seeking out supportive people and communities. No one grows alone, and having others in your corner can be a game-changer.
And give yourself permission to rest and renew. Growth isn’t always a straight line—it ebbs and flows, and that’s not just okay, it’s natural.
Now, think about how this shows up in real life. Maybe you’re standing up for yourself at work. Maybe you’ve picked up a new hobby, or maybe you’re just letting yourself enjoy a quiet moment of contentment.
Each time you choose to live out loud, you’re proving your own resilience and your worth.
Of course, the journey doesn’t just end here. There will be setbacks. There will be challenges. But with every step, you’re building a life that feels more true, more connected, and more empowered.
The practices you’ve learned—trusting yourself, taking care of yourself, being vulnerable, connecting with others, finding humor, setting boundaries, showing courage, being authentic, and practicing compassion—these aren’t just tools. They’re ways of being. And they have the power to transform not just your life, but the lives of everyone around you.
So, keep living out loud. The world needs what only you can bring.
